title: Asymmetric timeliness of earnings, market-to-book and conservatism in financial reporting

models.model_label: Future earnings timeliness by beginning-of-period MTB rank
models.sample_description: Compustat–CRSP firm-years over 1972–1999. The base sample requires MTB at year-end t and earnings and returns from t−4 through t+3; it excludes negative-book-value firms and truncates the top/bottom 0.5% of price-deflated annual and long-horizon earnings and returns. The reported 45,664 is the full sample aggregate, not the per-year cross-sectional N used for each horizon.
models.method_details: Fama–Macbeth cross-sectional estimation is reported; the estimator applied within each annual cross-section is not separately identified.
models.equation_text: E_{t+1,t+k}/P_t = a_0 + a_1 MTB_RANK_t + Z_0 DR_{t+1,t+k} + Z_1 MTB_RANK_t × DR_{t+1,t+k} + b_0 R_{t+1,t+k} + b_1 MTB_RANK_t × R_{t+1,t+k} + g_0 R_{t+1,t+k} × DR_{t+1,t+k} + g_1 MTB_RANK_t × R_{t+1,t+k} × DR_{t+1,t+k} + ε_t, k=1,2,3

fixed_effects.details: Fixed effects are not specified for the annual cross-sectional regressions.

standard_errors.details: The authors use the time series of annual cross-sectional coefficients over 1972–1999 to calculate the mean coefficient and associated t-statistics; no further standard-error correction is stated.

Long-horizon earnings are computed by adding annual earnings over the appropriate horizon. Similarly, long-horizon returns are calculated by compounding annual fiscal-year returns. For every firm-year with MTB available at the end of year t, we require availability of returns and earnings from time t�4 to time t+3. 3. Data


We begin with the intersection of all firm-years in COMPUSTAT and CRSP with
sufficient data to calculate income before extraordinary items (IBEI), market value of

equity (EV), book values and fiscal-year equity returns. Fiscal-year returns are 12-month
buy-and-hold returns beginning the fourth month of the fiscal year, consistent with Hayn
(1995) and Basu (1997). Long-horizon earnings are computed by adding annual earnings
over the appropriate horizon. Similarly, long-horizon returns are calculated by
compounding annual fiscal-year returns. For every firm-year with MTB available at the
end of year t, we require availability of returns and earnings from time t�4 to time t+3.
To reduce the effects of outliers, observations in the top or bottom 0.5% of price-deflated
annual and long-horizon earnings, as well as annual and long-horizon returns are
truncated. We exclude firms with negative book values. <sup>14</sup> The final sample consists of
45,664 firm-years over the period 1972–1999.
Table 1 presents the descriptive statistics for the earnings and returns data in our
sample over different horizons, along with statistics on the market value of equity
and MTB ratio. Rt+1,t+k and Et+1,t+k represent returns and earnings, respectively,
cumulated forward for every firm over the period t+1 to t+k, with k varying from 1 to 3.
Rt�j,t and Et�j,t represent returns and earnings, respectively, cumulated backward
for every firm over the period t�j to t, with j varying from 0 to 4. Mean returns
and earnings are increasing in horizon, as expected, as are their standard deviations.
The descriptive statistics for returns are very similar over matching horizons, irrespective
of the direction in which they are cumulated. The same is true for earnings. Minor
differences arise mechanically because the cumulative returns at the beginning and
at the end of the time series differ depending on whether the returns lag or lead with respect
to time t.
